headline: A health-policy group called PHTI says US healthcare payment rules push AI toward billing work instead of tools that improve patients' health, and wants payment changed.
score_reason: Relevant policy argument, but a group's recommendations relayed by one trade outlet.
importance_line: It argues that how hospitals and insurers are paid decides which AI gets built, which matters to patients and payers, though these are PHTI's recommendations, not decisions.
summary: HIT Consultant reports that PHTI, whose executive director is Caroline Pearson, has released a framework arguing that US payment rules reward administrative AI, citing an AI scribe linked to 5% more top-level visits and about $1,004 extra billing per doctor each month. PHTI recommends outcome-based payment and clearer liability rules so that AI which improves health, such as for high blood pressure, can be paid for.
notes: The article is written in an opinionated style and relays PHTI's report; PHTI's full report was not read.
